hypotheses.paper: U a CGHD of M and M', C ∩ J^+(ι(M)) ≠ ∅
hypotheses.note: CGHDData (package 5's A3 setting, ψ injective on U) + p₀ ∈ C ∩ J⁺(S); past twin with J⁻, K⁺ (no duality of the E₀ bundle, R4)

hypotheses.paper: design §3 step 4: minimise a Geroch time over ∂U ∩ J(Σ,p₀)
hypotheses.note: no time function: a causal-order-minimal point suffices (M causal, J⁻(x) closed, T2)

findings: Design §3 step 4 / §5 row 6 ('time function' risk) is void for Lemma 3.9: minimality for the causal order on the compact ∂U ∩ J⁺(Σ) ∩ J⁻(p₀) (Zorn on closed down-sets) replaces the Geroch time, and every boundary point below a corresponding point corresponds (K⁻ cluster argument). SingularGeroch need not be restated on the corrected bundle for this package.

labels.label: prop:Cauchy_point_min

hypotheses.paper: M0 GH singular flat, Cauchy extensions M1, M2, common sub-extension N
hypotheses.note: CGHDData over an abstract Geometry (DEC-60); ETT labels are the ETT campaign's

exists_diamond_subset_of_nonempty: ETT's literal statement at its own hypothesis C ≠ ∅ (future case by Lemma 3.9 + spacelike_iff; past case vacuous, p' = p₀: σ ≤ x ≤ p₀ ≤ σ' puts x in the diamond of σ, σ' ∈ S ⊆ U, so J⁺(S) ∩ J⁻(p₀) ⊆ U by causal convexity). exists_spacelike: Sbierski's time-oriented (3.10) in the future or the past of S (Sbierski's WLOG 'otherwise reverse the time orientation' made explicit, as E₀ has no time reversal). exists_diamond_subset: future side from C ∩ J⁺(S) ≠ ∅
equivalent for p ∈ ∂U (spacelike_iff: K⁻ density + lem:passe_pgcd)

findings: ETT.tex:2270-2274 is TRUE as stated (exists_diamond_subset_of_nonempty) but VACUOUS at past points: if p₀ ∈ C ∩ J⁻(Σ₁), then J⁺(Σ₁) ∩ J⁻(p₀) ⊆ j₁(N) by causal convexity, so p' = p₀ satisfies the conclusion with no information. It is therefore too weak to feed prop:Cauchy_non_max's past-side slice: what the proof of prop:Cauchy_non_max needs is the time-oriented form (Sbierski (3.10) in the future OR in the past of Σ₁, exists_spacelike). (Corrects this report's earlier wording, which said the statement 'should say in the future or in the past' as if it were false.)

ETT.tex:2275-2317 (editorial proof, '[editorial] translated … verify'): the procedure along broken lightlike geodesics and the finiteness argument via discreteness of Σ1 ∩ sing(M1) are not needed: a ≤-minimal point of the compact ∂j1(N) ∩ J(Σ1, p) does it (exists_spacelike_corresponding).

labels.label: sbierski:lem:3.11

hypotheses.paper: U a GHD, M ⊇ U an extension, p ∈ ∂U with (3.10), W an open neighbourhood
hypotheses.note: W any neighbourhood; only ⊆ of (3.10); model-free hypotheses (p ∈ Z⁺, J^±(x) closed, J⁻(p) ⊆ closure K⁻(p), lem:Sigma_separe's clause, compact J⁺(S) ∩ J⁻(x), U causally convex), all derived from A2 at Level A

hypotheses.paper: proof: a timelike curve γ from p, sequences, 'the relation ≤ is closed', 'contradicts the GH of U'
hypotheses.note: directed family q ≫ p, q ≤ q₁ (Z⁺) in a compact set; closed J⁺(r); final contradiction by K⁻ density + lem:passe_pgcd

exists_lt_Jplus_compl_subset_past asks p ∉ sing₀: at a BTZ point I⁻(p) = ∅ (Iminus_eq_empty, Geometry.lean:174), so the conclusion ∃ q ≪ p is unsatisfiable there; the past lemma without p ∉ sing₀ would assert that no BTZ boundary point satisfies its hypotheses (past (3.10), U GH) — not settled here, no local BTZ configuration exhibited either way

findings: Sbierski Lemma 3.11's past twin cannot conclude at BTZ points: I⁻(p) = ∅ there, so Sbierski's slice τ_q (q ∈ I^∓(p)) is unavailable on the past side at a BTZ boundary point. Whether a BTZ boundary point satisfying the past (3.10) with U GH exists is not settled here. Consequence for whoever discharges A4 (Geometry.slice_past) at the E₀ instance (packages 11/12, gx): Sbierski's construction cannot be time-reversed at BTZ points; a different slice is needed there (or an argument that a past-side (3.10) point is never BTZ).
questions: Does gx's discharge of A4 slice_past at BTZ points have a construction (Sbierski's τ_q needs q ≪ p, impossible at a BTZ point)? Lemma 3.11's past twin is proved here only at regular points.
